links.outcome: Landmark detection error under complex conditions (malocclusion, missing teeth, metal artifacts)
links.effect: Average MRE for SCT and CBCT below 1.3 mm, and below 1.4 mm in complex conditions such as malocclusion, missing dental landmarks, and metal artifacts.
links.quote: The average MRE for both SCT and CBCT was consistently below 1.3 mm and, notably, below 1.4 mm in complex conditions such as malocclusion, missing dental landmarks, and the presence of metal artifacts.

links.outcome: Performance difference between external multicenter and internal datasets (MRE, SDR)
links.effect: No significant differences in MRE and SDR at 2-4 mm between external and internal SCT and CBCT sets.
links.quote: No significant differences in MRE and SDR at 2-4 mm were observed between external and internal SCT and CBCT sets.

links.outcome: Specialists' landmarking accuracy and speed with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: AI assistance improved landmarking proficiency of senior and junior specialists by 15.9% and 28.9%, and sped the process 6 to 9.5 times.
links.quote: The implementation of this model significantly improved the landmarking proficiency of senior and junior specialists by 15.9% and 28.9%, respectively, while also accelerating the process by a factor of 6 to 9.5 times.

screen.reason: The study evaluates a 3D U-Net for cephalometric landmarking and performs a reader study measuring the impact of AI assistance on the proficiency and speed of junior and senior specialists compared to manual annotation.
